tools.name: os3d
tools.title: OpenShape 3D
tools.description: Everything in OpenShape 3D goes through this one tool, so the person approves it once. op names the operation and args carries its arguments (os3d.guide lists them all with units, axes and recipes; read it once before modelling). READS: 'health' (is the app reachable, is a design open — call first), 'guide' (the modelling guide), 'state' (every body with exact volume in mm3 and bounds, selection, undo state — verify geometry here, not in a picture), 'faces' and 'edges' with args {"body": id} (1-based kernel indices that shell, fillet, chamfer and the face ops take; re-list after every feature), 'sketches', 'check' with optional {"body", "bop": true} (is it a valid solid — run before exporting), 'screenshot' with optional {"width", "height"} (a JPEG of the viewport; wait a second after a view command), 'commands' (runnable command ids), 'accuracy' with {"reference": id, "model": id} (how closely the model body matches the reference body — a part built over an imported 3D scan against the scan: silhouette overlap per view, outline and surface deviation in mm both ways, a summary; optional "views", "tolerance" mm, "align" none|boundsCenter|base), 'accuracy.image' (the same with "view": one of front, top, right, back, bottom, left — a picture of the reference silhouette under the model's outline); 'view.deviationPreview' with {"reference": id, "model": id} colours the reference in the viewport by its distance to the model (blue where the model is missing material, orange where it has too much, grey within tolerance) and replies with the per-vertex numbers — take a 'screenshot' while it is on to see where a model is wrong, then {"off": true}. CHANGES, each recorded as an undoable feature exactly as if modelled by hand: 'sketch.create', 'sketch.addEntities', 'feature.extrude', 'feature.revolve', 'feature.loft', 'feature.sweep', 'feature.shell', 'feature.fillet', 'feature.chamfer', 'feature.boolean', 'feature.pattern', 'feature.mirror', 'feature.transform', 'feature.pushPull', the face ops, 'body.setMaterial', 'item.setHidden', 'item.rename' ({"id": body or sketch id, "name": text} — the name an exported file shows for that part), 'item.select' ({"ids": []} clears the selection — an import or feature leaves its result selected and tinted blue, so clear it before a picture); 'command.run' with {"id": "view.fit"} runs a view or undo/redo command (edit.undo reverts one feature); 'document.export' with {"format": "stl"|"3mf"|"obj"|"step"|"glb", "up": "z", "body": [ids], "name": "flowerpot"} saves a file to the person's Downloads folder (up='z' for a 3D-printing slicer; one printable part per file; the reply gives fileName, path and sizeMM). Units are millimetres and degrees. A feature reply carries the new state plus producedBodyIDs / changedBodyIDs / removedBodyIDs; 'failed': true means the feature was recorded but did not build — read 'message', run command.run edit.undo, and correct the arguments.

op.description: Operation name: health, guide, state, faces, edges, sketches, check, screenshot, commands, or a change such as feature.extrude, command.run, document.export.

args.description: The operation's arguments (omit for health, guide, state, sketches, commands).
